description: Canonical machine-readable description of the Helios command-gate contract. The validator (hooks/gate_check.ps1) reads required base fields from this file, and the virtual schema responder (hooks/helios_pretooluse.ps1) projects bounded slices of it over the HELIOS/1 wire protocol. Tier-required fields are live policy data in policy/command-policy.json and are merged into responses at answer time - they are deliberately not duplicated here.

versions.gate_documents: command-gate.v1 - the schema_version value every gate JSON in pending/ must declare, enforced by exact match; any other value (including '1.0' and 'helios-gate.v1') is denied with this canonical value in the response
versions.schema_document: helios-gate-schema.v1 - the version of this file
versions.wire_protocol: HELIOS/1 - every virtual response and real denial begins with a sentinel line 'HELIOS/1 VIRTUAL <op> <OK|ERROR>' or 'HELIOS/1 DENY <REASON_CODE>' followed by one line of compact JSON

virtual.rules: Exact grammar only. Pipes, redirection, chaining, inline interpreters, dynamic evaluation, encoded execution, and unrecognized arguments are rejected. These strings are protocol tokens intercepted by the verified front controller after integrity verification; nothing executes through PATH, no gate is consumed, and a 'HELIOS/1 VIRTUAL <op> OK' response is the answer - the command must not be retried.
virtual.size_budget: Responses target 4096 bytes, hard cap 8192; bare 'helios gate schema' returns only an index; every response carries 'truncated' and, when more data exists, a 'next' hint with the exact follow-up command

types_and_meaning.correlation_id: string - unique id for this gate; becomes the evidence correlation id and the chain predecessor for the next command
types_and_meaning.expires_utc: string - ISO-8601 UTC; expired gates are rejected
types_and_meaning.command: string - the EXACT command text the tool will execute, byte-for-byte
types_and_meaning.command_sha256: string - lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of command
types_and_meaning.working_directory: string - must equal the hook-observed effective working directory at retry time (for Codex this is the shell_command workdir)
types_and_meaning.risk_tier: integer 0-3 - must be >= the tier Helios detects for the command
types_and_meaning.exit_capture: string - see enums.exit_capture; mode 'suffix' requires the command to end with an approved suffix; 'not_applicable' additionally requires exit_capture_reason from the approved list
types_and_meaning.multi_command: boolean - true when the command decomposes into more than one segment
types_and_meaning.need: string - semantic: why this command is needed (agent-authored, never scaffolded)
types_and_meaning.expected: string - semantic: what output/effect is expected
types_and_meaning.actual_means: string - semantic: what the command actually does mechanically
types_and_meaning.next_logic: string - semantic: what happens next depending on the result
types_and_meaning.stop_conditions: string[] - required at tier >= 2 (live policy): conditions under which execution must be aborted
types_and_meaning.read_write_impact: object - required at tier 3 and under write/capability detection; see section 'impact'
types_and_meaning.exit_capture_reason: string - required when exit_capture='not_applicable'; see enums.exit_capture_reason
types_and_meaning.data_sha256: string - terminal write fields; see section 'terminal_write'
types_and_meaning.terminal_id: string - terminal write fields; see section 'terminal_write'
types_and_meaning.enter: boolean - terminal write fields; see section 'terminal_write'

enums.approval_boundary_note: approval_boundary is validated as non-empty free text, not an enum. Recommended vocabulary: describe what the command may touch and what it must not (e.g. 'read-only diagnostics; no writes, no network').

tiers.0: routine - no pattern match; gate still required
tiers.1: diagnostic - read-only inspection commands (ls, cat, grep, Get-*)
tiers.2: remote/admin - ssh, sudo, service control, UI automation
tiers.3: modifying - file mutation, git push/reset, package installs, process control
tiers.4: forbidden - unconditionally blocked; CANNOT be authorized by any gate
tiers.tier_required_fields: LIVE POLICY DATA - resolved from policy/command-policy.json (tier_required_fields) at answer time and merged into schema responses; not duplicated in this file
tiers.capability_escalation: Inline interpreters (bash -c, python -c, -Command), dynamic eval (eval, Invoke-Expression), and encoded execution escalate to tier 3 and require read_write_impact + stop_conditions; nested shell/command substitution ($(...), backticks) escalates to tier 2 and requires read_write_impact

segments.contract: Any command containing a separator outside quotes must declare multi_command:true and segments[] listing every segment in order, trimmed, duplicates included. Declared segments must exactly equal the detected decomposition or the gate is rejected with SEGMENT MISMATCH.
segments.quote_awareness: Separators inside single-quoted or double-quoted spans are not split; a backslash-escaped quote does not toggle quoting. Limitations (honest): PowerShell backtick escapes and here-strings are not modeled - here-string markers set ambiguous_parse, which at tier 0 requires explicit read_write_impact.
segments.wrapper_exemption: Commands with exit_capture='wrapper_required' are exempt from chain detection; the wrapper identity fields protect against hidden actions instead

chain.contract: Once a session has prior executable evidence (a posttooluse_evidence_written ledger entry), every subsequent gate must declare exactly one of: previous_correlation_id (the correlation id of the most recent executed command - provided as last_correlation_id in denial responses) or new_chain:true (explicitly starting an unrelated chain). They are mutually exclusive statements of chain intent.
chain.virtual_note: virtual_op_answered ledger events are continuity-neutral: they never become the chain predecessor and never require linkage

impact.contract: read_write_impact must be an object with reads[] and writes[] arrays (string forms are rejected). Required at tier 3, when a write indicator matches the command, or when a capability flag (inline execution, dynamic eval, encoded execution, nested shell) is active. writes:['none'] is valid ONLY when nothing requires write disclosure; under write/capability detection it is rejected.
impact.ttl_note: List concrete paths or path classes, not vague categories

wrapper.when: exit_capture='wrapper_required' - the command wraps the real operation so the true exit code is captured as output (EXIT=<code>) while the tool itself exits 0, guaranteeing PostToolUse evidence
wrapper.validators: LIVE POLICY DATA - wrapper_validators in policy/command-policy.json define per-shell must_contain and must_end_with strings the full command must satisfy

identity_fields.wrapped_command: the semantic command being measured; must appear literally inside the full command
identity_fields.wrapped_command_sha256: SHA-256 of wrapped_command (UTF-8); recomputed and compared at validation
identity_fields.wrapper_reason: why the wrapper is needed (typically: nonzero exit is expected diagnostic output that must be captured)

terminal_write.when: The command targets CODEAPI /term/:id/write. Required for all terminal write commands; rejected on any other command.

fields.data_sha256: SHA-256 of the write payload's data field (UTF-8); the agent declares the expected hash, the hook extracts data from the command AST (Parser.ParseInput) and rejects on mismatch
fields.terminal_id: the terminal identifier from the write URI path (/term/<terminal_id>/write); extracted from the -Uri parameter by the hook and compared against the gate declaration
fields.enter: boolean; whether the write appends a CR; extracted from the -Body hashtable by the hook and compared against the gate declaration

terminal_write.verification: The hook always overwrites the gate's declared values with the AST-extracted values before moving to inflight. An agent-declared hash that does not match the actual command is rejected. If extraction fails (unparseable command, missing parameter), the gate is rejected — the hook never passes an unverifiable write through.
terminal_write.codeapi_guard: CODEAPI's gate_guard.py independently checks inflight gates against the actual HTTP write payload (data_sha256, terminal_id, enter, expires_utc). A write that bypassed the hook (fetch, node_repl) has no matching gate in inflight and gets 403.

ttl.contract: created_utc and expires_utc are ISO-8601 UTC. Expired gates are rejected. Gates are single-use: on successful validation the gate file moves from pending/ to inflight/ and cannot authorize a second execution. Recommended TTL: at most 24 hours; scaffolds suggest 1 hour.

scaffold.contract: The scaffold is informational only: it never writes to pending/, never authorizes a command, never consumes a gate, never executes a process. The requesting agent must author every semantic field and choose its chain intent explicitly, then write the completed gate to pending/ itself.
scaffold.binding: Scaffolds resolve only session-bound blocked records no older than 30 minutes belonging to the requesting session; legacy records without a session id return STALE_RECORD
scaffold.destination_discovery: Every successful scaffold response also returns the absolute gate_root, pending_directory, suggested_gate_filename (literal <correlation-id>.gate.json), suggested_gate_path, and a write_instruction, so an agent that has never seen the Helios root learns exactly where to write the completed gate. These paths derive solely from the front controller's own gate root and cannot be redirected by blocked-record contents; write the completed gate to suggested_gate_path, never relative to the current working directory. Real GATE_REQUIRED denials also carry gate_root, pending_directory, scaffold_command, and suggested_gate_path when a scaffold is available.

tier_3_powershell_delta.note: tier 3 additionally requires (live policy): stop_conditions[] and read_write_impact {reads:[], writes:[]}; write indicators make writes:['none'] invalid; commands must still end with an approved exit-capture suffix for the declared shell
